canonical_seed.solution_text: “Naturally more energetic” is undefined and does not specify an observable test of the cause.

canonical_seed.student_text:
A student models a small fan cart with Δv = kF for the same push time. Use the data to decide whether the model is supported and explain what the relationship means physically.

Force F (N): 2 | 4 | 6
Change in speed Δv (m/s): 0.5 | 1.0 | 1.6
canonical_seed.student_html:
A student models a small fan cart with Δv = kF for the same push time. Use the data to decide whether the model is supported and explain what the relationship means physically.

Force F (N): 2 | 4 | 6
Change in speed Δv (m/s): 0.5 | 1.0 | 1.6
canonical_seed.answer: The model is supported approximately: doubling/tripling force produces about double/triple change in speed. Physically, for the same push duration and cart, a larger net force produces a larger velocity change.
canonical_seed.solution_text: The model is supported approximately: doubling/tripling force produces about double/triple change in speed. Physically, for the same push duration and cart, a larger net force produces a larger velocity change.

canonical_seed.student_text:
A spacecraft coasts far from large bodies with its engine off. Its measured velocity stays 320 m/s east. Which explanation is consistent with Newton’s First Law?
A. A constant eastward force is required to maintain the velocity.
B. The net force can be zero while the spacecraft keeps constant velocity.
C. Inertia is an eastward force.
D. Zero net force requires zero speed.
canonical_seed.student_html:
A spacecraft coasts far from large bodies with its engine off. Its measured velocity stays 320 m/s east. Which explanation is consistent with Newton’s First Law?

  1. A constant eastward force is required to maintain the velocity.
  2. The net force can be zero while the spacecraft keeps constant velocity.
  3. Inertia is an eastward force.
  4. Zero net force requires zero speed.
choices: A constant eastward force is required to maintain the velocity.
The net force can be zero while the spacecraft keeps constant velocity.
Zero net force requires zero speed.
canonical_seed.answer: B — The net force can be zero while the spacecraft keeps constant velocity.
canonical_seed.solution_text: Zero net force produces no change in velocity; motion can continue at constant velocity.
canonical_seed.solution_html: Zero net force produces no change in velocity; motion can continue at constant velocity.

C. Inertia replaces friction when mass is added.
D. Only moving objects have inertia.

Inertia replaces friction when mass is added.
